High Court Of Chhattisgarh, Bilaspur
 Order Sheet
CRA No. 1029 of 2021   Radhelal Kanwar S/o Tilakram Aged About 45 Years R/o- Village -  Kudhritar, P.S. Nagarda, District Janjgir-Champa (Chhattisgarh)

---- Appellant  Versus   State Of Chhattisgarh Through - Police Station Nagarda, District  Janjgir-Champa (Chhattisgarh)
 ---- Respondent (Cause-title taken from Case Information System) 15/03/2024

Mr. Shashi Bhushan Tiwari,
Advocate for the appellant.
Mr. Khulesh Sahu, Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State.

Heard on I.A. No. 01/2024, an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.
This is a 3rd bail application submitted by the appellant.
First bail application was dismissed as withdrawn on 14.02.2022 and second bail application was dismissed as withdrawn on 01.08.2023.

By the impugned judgment dated 03.09.2021, passed by learned Special Judge (FTSC), Sakti,
District Janjgir-Champa, Chhattisgarh, in Sessions Case No. 35/2019, appellant stands convicted for the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(<+) of Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years and fine of Rs.1000/- with default stipulation.

entities.text:
Special Judge (FTSC), Sakti,
District Janjgir-Champa, Chhattisgarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that without any sufficient cause and material, the trial Court has wrongly convicted the appellant.
He submits that it is a case of false implication where the victim, who is a married lady, has falsely implicated the appellant.
As per the prosecution story itself at the time of incident, she was gone to the appellant's home for her treatment along with her husband.

Referring to Ex.P/1 i.e. report lodged by the appellant, counsel submits that at the time of alleged incident, the husband of victim was present there in drunk condition and there was a dispute (maarpeet) taken place between both of them, therefore, firstly the accused lodged a report against the husband of victim, and thereafter, present FIR has been lodged by the victim against appellant,
which clearly shows that on the false implication upon the appellant, the FIR has been lodged.

Lastly, he submits that appellant is in jail since 03.09.2021 and the appeal is likely to take more time to finalize, therefore, it is prayed by the counsel that the appellant may be granted benefit of bail and Radhelal Kanwar vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146229171/
1

sentences.text: his sentence may also be suspended.
On the other hand, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the State opposes the arguments and supports the judgment of conviction.
He submits that taking into the consideration the statement of victim, the trial Court has rightly convicted the appellant.
I have heard both the counsel, perused the evidence submitted by the prosecution before the trial Court.

Considering the rival submissions made by both the counsel, particularly considering the fact that firstly FIR has been lodged by the appellant against the husband of victim and thereafter the victim lodged the FIR.
Without further expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am inclined to grant benefit of bail to the appellant Accordingly, I.A. No. 01/2024 stands allowed.

It is directed that the substantive jail sentence imposed upon the appellant shall remain suspended during the pendency of this appeal and he shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs. 50,000/- with one solvent surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 12th of June, 2024.

He shall thereafter appear before the Trial Court on a date given by the Registry of this Court and shall continue to appear there on all such subsequent dates as are given to him by the said Court, till disposal of this appeal.
List this case for final hearing in due course.

Sd/-
